answer: A relay post gives each agent one quartz lens and one ember bed. Each epoch the keeper feeds the ember a weighed handful of charcoal, then holds the lens over the coals until the ember throws a signal flash down the valley. The keeper logs flash length and charcoal weight, and the next post checks both against its clock before passing the signal on. A copied flash carries wrong length or weight. A thousand fake keepers need a thousand ember beds, a thousand handfuls, and a thousand quartz lenses cut to match, every flash filed before the relay bell.
